route: none available for the item axis (no item text shipped); instrument-identity check via published scale mean/SD/alpha
evidence: No item text was shipped (blocked on source availability), so no item_text<->item mapping reaches the corpus; NO_ROUTE rather than NOT_NEEDED because mapping_basis is unknown and only data_labels is exempt. What the data DOES establish, and what verify_GBJW_fadplus_goto2021.R re-runs, is instrument identity and keying, not item identity: the seven GBJW_1..7 columns give a respondent-mean scale score of 3.195 (SD 0.691) over all 802 rows of FAD_compare_rawdata.csv against the paper's published 3.220 (SD 0.706, alpha 0.773) for 'Beliefs in a just world' -- a 0.025 gap attributable to the paper's data cleaning -- while the FAD-Plus blocks in the same file are 27 items on a 1-5 scale, so the table holds the GBJW and not the instrument its name implies. Raw-score alpha computed on the same seven columns is 0.778 against the published 0.773, confirming the items are stored raw and positively keyed (all seven GBJW items are positively worded, so no reverse-scoring question arises). What this does NOT establish: which of Lipkus's seven items each code refers to. Every route in Step 5b is unavailable here -- no per-item statistics are published (route 1), all seven items share one 1-6 range (route 2), the scale is unidimensional with no subscales (routes 3 and 5), no parameter is implied by the item text (route 4), no reverse-keyed items exist to separate polarity classes (route 6), no marker item is predicted (route 7), and the per-item means 3.693/3.771/3.483/2.677/3.711/2.657/2.372 leave items 1, 2 and 5 within 0.08 of one another (3.771/3.711/3.693) and items 4 and 6 within 0.020 (2.677/2.657), so even a semantic-coherence argument (route 8) could not separate them. Re-run: verify_GBJW_fadplus_goto2021.R reproduces this against the live table (802 complete respondents, mean 3.195 vs 3.220, SD 0.691 vs 0.706, alpha 0.778 vs 0.773; the reversed-scoring counterfactual would give 3.805) and ends VERDICT: PASS, where PASS means the instrument-identity and keying claim reproduces, not that any wording was verified. The option axis (route 9) needs no inference: the paper states the anchors and the source file already stores 1-6 integers.

Route 5 (subscale block structure) on the study's own data.sav, which reproduces the live per-item means exactly (CAnxiety1 3.50, CAnxiety2 3.99, CAnxiety3 3.45; n=459 each) so the source columns are the ones behind the live item codes. Within-anxiety correlations 0.46/0.70/0.53 vs anxiety-by-avoidance 0.05-0.34: min within 0.46 > max cross 0.34, so the three shipped worry statements belong to the CAnxiety block and not to the six avoidance statements. This does NOT distinguish CAnxiety1, 2 and 3 from each other - all three share the 1-7 range and near-identical worry content, the deposit publishes no per-item statistics, and the reverse-worded avoidance items are already reverse-scored in the file (CAvoidance2/4 correlate +0.46/+0.42 with CAvoidance1), so the polarity route is unavailable too. Within-block order rests on the questionnaire's own item order; note r(CAnxiety1,CAnxiety3)=0.70 > r(CAnxiety2,CAnxiety3)=0.53 although questionnaire items 8 and 9 are the content-nearest pair, which is mild non-corroboration rather than evidence of a permutation.

Route 5, SIWB published subscale split (items 1-6 Self-Efficacy, 7-12 Life Scheme) tested against the live correlation matrix (n=459, 12 items): all 12/12 items' most-correlated partner lies in their own subscale (e.g. SWB1->SWB4 r=0.446, SWB6->SWB4 r=0.305, SWB7->SWB9 r=0.467, SWB10->SWB11 r=0.372, SWB12->SWB9 r=0.404); within-block mean r=0.333 (30 pairs) vs cross-block 0.277 (36 pairs). This pins block membership and rules out any mapping that moves an item across the two subscales. It does NOT distinguish items within a block (a SWB3/SWB5 swap would be invisible), and it does not test the anchor direction, so PARTIAL. Supporting, non-statistical: data/gao2025_family_support.py melts .sav columns by name so item code = source column name, and Section IV is the questionnaire's only 12-item 1-5 block.

Exempt: the source .sav's own variable labels tie each ERQ code to its text (ERQ1 -> '1. When I want to feel more of a positive emotion...'), the IRW item code IS that source column name (data/garciabatista_2021_erq_covid_healthworkers.py melts ITEM_COLS=['ERQ1'..'ERQ10'] unchanged), so no inference was made for statistics to check. Corroborated anyway by route 3 (published subscale totals): the paper reports M=3.45 across the cognitive reappraisal items and M=2.93 across the suppression items; averaging the live per-item means for the canonical ERQ split gives reappraisal (ERQ1 3.34, ERQ3 3.53, ERQ5 3.70, ERQ7 3.32, ERQ8 3.43, ERQ10 3.53) = 3.475 and suppression (ERQ2 3.14, ERQ4 2.58, ERQ6 2.92, ERQ9 3.09) = 2.9325, matching to 0.025 and 0.0025 respectively. That corroboration pins subscale MEMBERSHIP only; it does not distinguish order within either subscale -- the variable labels do, which is why this row is NOT_NEEDED rather than PARTIAL.

route: route 9 (response-frequency matching vs deposit .sav labels) + route 3 (published subscale alphas)
evidence: ROUTE 9 + ROUTE 3, both computed this run. Route 9: the deposit .sav stores label strings while the IRW table stores 1-4, so per-item x per-level counts were compared: all 120 cells (30 items x 4 levels) match exactly, e.g. asignationpatients 16/33/89/131 sav vs 16/33/89/131 live, relationsnursphysic 7/23/125/114 vs 7/23/125/114, enoughworkers 74/79/69/47 vs 74/79/69/47; 0 mismatched items, and all 30 count signatures are DISTINCT, so no pair of items could be swapped and no level permuted without breaking it. This pins both axes: every live item column is uniquely tied to its .sav source column, and resp 1=absolutely disagree ... 4=absolutely agree is the .sav's own value labelling. Route 3: recomputed Cronbach alpha per PES-NWI dimension from the items this file assigns to each, against the paper's published values -- D1 0.877 vs 0.87, D2 0.839 vs 0.85 (9 items, item 18 absent from the IRW table), D3 0.938 vs 0.93, D4 0.849 vs 0.84, D5 0.813 vs 0.81, whole scale 0.941 vs published 0.943 for all 31 items; largest deviation 0.011. Text tie itself rests on the .sav labels 'item 1'..'item 31' plus the numbered supplement, corroborated item by item by the self-describing codes. What this does NOT establish: no statistic here reads the Spanish sentence, so a hypothetical error inside the deposit's own numbering (label says 'item 10' but the questionnaire's item 10 is a different sentence) would survive both routes; the code-name/wording correspondence is what rules that out, and it holds for all 30. verify_geacaballero_2019_pes_nwi.R re-runs both routes.
